questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to detect fixed bit patterns with pure bitwise ops, no loops or conditionals, reinforcing shifts, masking, and truthiness evaluation.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise shifts align neighboring bits
- Combining with AND tests multiple bit conditions simultaneously
- Pure bitwise approach scales to fixed-width inputs without branching

## Code Example
```c
bool hasPattern101(uint32_t n) {
  return (n & (n >> 2) & ~(n >> 1)) != 0;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for 64-bit inputs?
- What edge cases exist near the topmost bits (i=29) and how does masking affect them?

Assesses pattern recognition and solid bit-twiddling under time pressure.

- Using XOR with shifted version to collapse pattern
- Detecting all-ones masks with (x & (x+1)) == 0

}

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to use parallel bit manipulation to detect patterns without explicit iteration.

## Key Concepts
- Shift and AND reduction across offset windows
- Boundary-free detection across all 32 bits
- Branchless core logic

## Code Example
```c
int hasRunOf4Ones32(uint32_t x) {
    uint32_t t = x & (x >> 1) & (x >> 2) & (x >> 3);
    return t != 0;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this to handle 64-bit inputs?
- How does this perform with common compilers under various optimization levels?

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests precise bit-level reasoning and avoids expensive operations in tight loops, useful in storage engines and query optimizers.
